title: Bounding Box Filter
description:
You have a table of worldwide airports as points. Return all airports that fall inside the bounding box of Western Europe: longitudes -10° to 20°, latitudes 35° to 60°.

Goal

Return iata_code and airport_name, ordered by iata_code.

Example Output

iata_code  airport_name
---------  ----------------------
CDG        Charles de Gaulle
FRA        Frankfurt Airport
LHR        Heathrow Airport
schema:
Table: airports

ColumnTypeDescription
iata_codeVARCHAR3-letter IATA code
airport_nameVARCHARFull name
geomGEOMETRYPoint (lng, lat)

Tip: create the bounding box with ST_MakeEnvelope(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) and test with ST_Intersects.
hints:
💡 Hint 1 ST_MakeEnvelope(-10, 35, 20, 60) creates the bounding box polygon.
💡 Hint 2 You can also use ST_X(geom) BETWEEN -10 AND 20 AND ST_Y(geom) BETWEEN 35 AND 60.
starterCode:
LOAD spatial;

-- Return airports inside the Western Europe bounding box.
-- Longitudes -10 to 20, latitudes 35 to 60.
-- Return: iata_code, airport_name ordered by iata_code
SELECT

FROM airports
WHERE

ORDER BY iata_code;
setup:
CREATE TABLE airports AS SELECT * FROM (VALUES
  ('CDG', 'Charles de Gaulle',   ST_Point(2.55,   49.01)),
  ('FRA', 'Frankfurt Airport',   ST_Point(8.57,   50.03)),
  ('LHR', 'Heathrow Airport',    ST_Point(-0.46,  51.48)),
  ('JFK', 'John F. Kennedy',     ST_Point(-73.78, 40.63)),
  ('DXB', 'Dubai Intl',          ST_Point(55.36,  25.25)),
  ('NRT', 'Narita Intl',         ST_Point(140.39, 35.76)),
  ('MAD', 'Adolfo Suárez',       ST_Point(-3.57,  40.47)),
  ('AMS', 'Schiphol',            ST_Point(4.76,   52.31))
) t(iata_code, airport_name, geom);
